doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A Montreux trio with Dizzy Gillespie and its drummer
summary: Toots recalls a drummer he calls Mr. Soul in a Dizzy trio and meeting him again at North Sea.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then I saw that you had done a date with Dannie Richmond, of course known with Charles Mingus.
No, but my revelation was we’re not [inaudible].
And me on guitar and Dizzy. I think that’s what... three.
Yeah, he was doing a trio.

A trio. And I said, and he’s the number soul, Mr. Soul, that… [makes sound] rockin’ with him. And he sounded, again, like relatively to be compared with Elvin, you know. [imitating] And I was playing the guitar then. I… And each, we met lately about a few months ago at the… in Holland at the North Sea Jazz something.
And he was there with a workshop or something. And he looked… “Hey,” you know. He just about like Richard Tee. “How ya doin’, Junior?” [laughs]
Yeah. That’s great. Hey, you, you, you’re doing your homework.
